text:
aj: Quick RFC follow-up re: edge admission window semantics. I sketched a behavior we can implement without changing the runtime: early-accept (give a commit token), otherwise NACK with retry hint. Want feedback on tradeoffs for streaming partial responses and idempotency boundaries.

sara: high-level sounds good. can you outline the exact lifecycle you expect for a single request? especially what 'early-accept' means for KV cache and kv-cache warmup.

aj: sure. proposal: 1) ingress validates request, computes cost estimate, and either ACCEPT or REJECT. 2) ACCEPT returns a short-lived commit token in header: `X-RW-Commit: <token>` and starts streaming. 3) If downstream fails mid-stream, we use the token to rehydrate partial state (if possible) or fallback to a cheaper model variant using the token as idempotency.

bharat: whoa the rehydrate bit is tricky. we don't persist KV cache per request today. Are you proposing storing checkpoints per-token? that's expensive.

aj: not full checkpoints. think of the token as a logical pointer: if the runtime scheduled the request on a node with a cold cache, we accept and prime cache as we stream. token lets the gateway signal another node to continue by requesting cached prefixes from the origin node for a short window (30s). cheap in-memory checkpointing, TTL'd.

maya: so token acts as a session lease. what happens when token TTL expires mid-stream? do we abort or fallback?

aj: fallback path: the gateway can 1) restart from scratch on a compatible model variant (quantized/shorter context) or 2) return `partial=true` trailer so clients can choose to resume with the commit token (if they saved it). Default: automatic fallback to variant model with degraded latency profile.

sara: how do we ensure idempotency for POST-like requests? token shouldn't mean "we already charged" or produced side-effect twice.

aj: keep side-effect semantics outside token. tokens only bind to inference state. side-effects must be guarded by application-level idempotency keys (X-App-Idempotency). we should document recommended patterns: app idempotency + commit token for streaming resumption.

bharat: ok. metrics/observability question: we need clear counters for ACCEPTED/EARLY_ACCEPT/REJECT, RESUME_SUCCESS/RESUME_FAIL, and FALLBACK_USED. otherwise hard to attribute cost spikes.

maya: agree. Also add a gauge for token-lease-count and a histogram for resume-latency.

aj: noted. I'll add those. also thinking of a simple header contract: `X-RW-Accept: verdict=accept|reject; token=<uuid>; ttl_s=30; variant=xxx` example below: 

```
X-RW-Accept: verdict=accept; token=9f2a3b; ttl_s=30; variant=redwood-medium-q4
```

aj: If verdict=reject we include `retry_after` and `policy_hint` (eg `backoff`, `queue`) so caller knows whether to queue client-side.

sara: one more thing: streaming trailers. We should add a final trailer that includes `resume_possible=true|false` and `used_fallback=true|false` and `tokens_used=[...]`. helps debug partial responses.

bharat: +1. also recommend we cap token rehydrate attempts to 1 by default to avoid cascading load.

maya: security: tokens could be abused. make them short-lived, bound to origin IP and signed by KMS. also rate-limit resume attempts per-token.

aj: agreed. token will be HMAC-signed and TTL'd. resume endpoints validate signature + origin match.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: edge-gateway/accept-token-proto v0.1 -> staging at 2026-03-20T09:12:00Z :rocket:

sara: scoring tradeoffs: pros: quicker failure visibility, faster tail for many requests; cons: added complexity in gateway and potential memory pressure from token store. we should simulate with synthetic traces before rollout.

aj: plan: prototype in staging behind feature flag, run 24h perf test with heavy cold-cache tails and 48h soak on canary. I'll write up the follow-up RFC with config knobs and metrics.

\bmaya: ack, please include a diagram of state transitions (ACCEPT -> STREAMING -> RESUME -> FALLBACK/COMPLETE). small one pager will help infra and security signoff.

aj: will do. thanks all. :thumbsup:
